comparison: Both address dataset creation and characteristics (C1, C17-C19, C23-C24, C80-C91). OpenEval finds the methodology well-documented and SUPPORTED, while peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, explicitly noting 'the variation in the database with regards to individuals, background, source/setting is not clearly articulated' despite praising the dataset as 'important' and 'terrific.'

Both evaluate performance comparisons between models trained on different datasets (C2, C20-C21, C28-C34). Both find the claims SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm the finding, stating the authors 'demonstrate the value of their dataset' and show 'the model trained on their dataset had the best performance.'

Both address UMAP clustering and locomotion interpretations (C25-C27). Both find the claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the interpretation is 'reasonable given established biological knowledge' with appropriate cautious language. Peer reviewers accept the dataset characterization as 'mostly well described' without contesting these observations.

Both evaluate cross-species generalization from humans vs monkeys to apes (C35). Both find SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers explicitly highlight this as a strength, noting it provides 'evidence for an important consideration in the field' regarding phylogenetic similarity.

Both address conclusions about limited cross-species generalization (C62-C63, with C61 in OpenEval only). Both find SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers praise the phylogenetic similarity findings as demonstrating 'convincing potential' and providing important evidence for the field.

Both evaluate species-specific training benefits and phylogenetic effects (C3, C43-C44, C51-C52, with additional claims C45-C47 in OpenEval). Both find SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers praise the 'ablation experiments' as providing 'solid evidence that their large, specialized dataset is uniquely positioned to aid in pose estimation.'

Both evaluate decimation/sample efficiency experiments (C40-C42). Both find SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers explicitly praise these experiments as reflecting 'an important property of pose estimation systems' and revealing 'important insights about scaling properties.'

Both address comparative performance with other datasets (C22, C36-C39). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to confounding factors and speculative explanations, while peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, accepting the comparative metrics without challenge and noting the work 'rigorously tested the utility of this database.'

Both evaluate species-specific performance differences (C48-C50, with additional claims C45-C47 in peer review). Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the gibbon difficulty explanation is 'reasonable inference though not experimentally tested.' Peer reviewers accept the findings through their endorsement of ablation studies.

Both address architectural choice of HRNet-W48 (C53-C55). Both find SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers explicitly note the sample efficiency experiments reveal 'important insights about scaling properties of different model architectures, finding that HRNet saturates in performance improvements.'

Both evaluate dataset limitations (C68-C69, C71-C74). OpenEval finds limitations clearly stated and SUPPORTED, while peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, explicitly stating 'the variation in the database with regards to individuals, background, source/setting is not clearly articulated,' indicating the characterization needs improvement.

Both address dataset diversity and comparative claims (C56-C58, C70). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with the caveat that 'diversity' is not quantitatively defined. Peer review R1 addresses these claims as part of broader dataset characterization rated UNCERTAIN due to insufficient articulation of variation.

Both address anticipated use and broader impact (C59, C64-C67 in OpenEval; C59, C61, C67, C75-C79 in peer review). Both find SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers affirm the dataset 'will be important for many applications' and is 'likely to have a significant impact on both computer vision and animal behavior.'

Both address ethical considerations and potential applications (C75-C79). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting claims about tracking replacing brain measures are 'highly speculative.' Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, accepting the ethical and practical motivations without challenge as part of broader impact assessment.

OpenEval evaluates background claims about pose estimation and existing work (C4-C11) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these introductory/background claims.
OpenEval evaluates taxonomic and motivational background claims (C12-C16) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval evaluates methodological details including bootstrap methods and dataset preparation (C92-C95, C97) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific methodological implementation details.
